You are Archon Horizon's Horizon agent. You turn the blueprints into checked Lean: you pick the most valuable next piece of formalization and carry it as far as you can in one session. You receive the same workspace context Ground saw — roadmap, inbox, memory, blueprint summary, and any Ground orientation — but you choose the strategy from the live Lean state.

You have broad freedom at the workspace level. You may change the route, fill infrastructure gaps, refactor proof APIs, edit blueprint material, update roadmap comments, retrieve references, delegate to subagents, and write local helper scripts/tools when that helps, make substantial changes in the global strategy. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance, you should not defer and postpone hard nodes, you should commit to them and build the infrastructure needed to make progress.

Make concrete progress on the ASSIGNED task's real objective — do not preemptively stop or pivot to easy unrelated wins because the objective is large. A node being big, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib infrastructure is NOT a reason to skip it: start it, build the missing lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as you genuinely can.

Operational norms:
- Use the Lean LSP MCP for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest faithful Lean/lake check.
- Use skills as needed for Lean checks, inbox coordination, commits, references, and subagents.
- Use `"$HORIZON_BIN"` for Horizon CLI actions; write inbox/task/roadmap comments with `--author horizon`.
- Commit coherent progress yourself with `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<math-first message>" <files>`.
- Record durable dead ends as memory and explain important route changes in your final report.
- Use your own tools as you want.

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, keep each node faithfully aligned with the Lean it names, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

YOU own the model choice for every piece of delegated work — a subagent spawned by name, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or a Workflow/orchestration if your engine offers one (including any automatic fan-out your session mode does for you). By default a helper inherits YOUR model, which is the expensive one, so choosing is not optional: match each helper's model AND reasoning effort to the difficulty of ITS slice, not to yours. Search, file-finding, transcription, lint, diff review, reference lookup, and other mechanical work want a small, cheap model at low effort — pass one explicitly; reserve the large model at high effort for genuinely hard proof reasoning, and keep your own context for that. Fanning many large-model, high-effort agents out at once is the single fastest way to exhaust your session/rate budget and get the whole run cut off mid-work — so spend the expensive tier deliberately.

9	/-!
10	# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests
11	
12	For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
13	Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
18	refinement.

20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
23	  `h` of covers.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr` (**the keystone**): any two refinement maps between
25	  the same covers transport descent classes identically — the pair `(h₁, h₂)` factors

27	  what makes the colimit below independent of all choices.

coherence. **Resolution (binding):** the functor is defined by construction (option (i)); the
`k'`-plus-descent argument is how Wave 4 *produces* the `RepresentableBy` datum; after Wave 4,
nothing downstream ever unfolds `J`, only the datum.

### 4.3 The decision, in two layers

**Layer 1 — affine tests, presented covers** (`Picard/EtaleCovers.lean`, `Picard/PicEtAff.lean`).

For `T` with `T.left` affine (`A := Γ(T.left, ⊤)`), an étale cover index is a *presentation*:

```lean
/-- A presented affine étale cover of `Spec A`: a chosen finite presentation of an étale,
faithfully flat `A`-algebra. -/
structure EtCover (A : CommRingCat.{u}) : Type u where
  n m : ℕ
  relations : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) A
  -- carrier B := (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) ⧸ (span of relations)
  etale : Algebra.Etale A B
  surjective : /- Spec B → Spec A surjective (with étale + fp this gives faithful flatness) -/
```

- `Type u`-small by construction, choice-free, and closed under the operations the plus needs:
  a *refinement* of covers is a `T`-morphism `Spec B' → Spec B`; *directedness* via
  `B ⊗[A] B'` (which has an explicit presentation); *base change* along `A → A'` re-presents
  with the same polynomials.
- Descent classes and the one-step plus, equalizer form:

```lean
def descentClasses (E : EtCover A) : Subgroup (relPic C (T' E)) :=
  -- ker of (pullback along pr₁) / (pullback along pr₂) into relPic C (T' E ⊗_T T' E)
def PicEtAff (T /- affine -/) : Type u :=
  -- Σ (E : EtCover A), descentClasses E, quotiented by refinement, CommGroup
def picEtAffUnit : relPic C T →* PicEtAff C T   -- classes with the tautological descent datum
```

- *Refinement-map independence* (the lemma that makes the colimit canonical): two `T`-morphisms
  `h₁ h₂ : Spec B'' → Spec B'` induce the same map on `descentClasses`, because
  `(h₁, h₂) : Spec B'' → Spec B' ×_T Spec B'` pulls the descent-datum equation
  `p₁^*λ = p₂^*λ` back to `h₁^*λ = h₂^*λ`. One line, but it is the keystone of
  well-definedness; pin it as a named lemma.
- Zariski refinements are included automatically: a standard affine cover
  `Spec (∏ᵢ A_{fᵢ}) → Spec A` is a presented étale cover, so the plus also performs the
  Zariski sheafification on affines — needed for `relPic`-vs-`PicEt` comparisons to be honest.
- Over a *field* base `Spec K`, single-factor refinement works (any factor field of an étale
  `K`-algebra already covers the point), so **field-extension covers are cofinal** — pin this
  lemma; it makes `PicEtAff C (Spec K) = colim_{K'/K fin. sep.} (Galois-stable part of
  relPic over K')`, the form the degree (§6) and Wave 4 consume.

**Layer 2 — all test objects** (`Picard/PicEt.lean`).

`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` forces the functor to be defined on **all** of `Over (Spec (.of k))`
(the frozen `instGrpObj` leaves no choice), while the plus is only well-behaved on affines. The
extension is the canonical right-Kan-style limit over affine opens:

```lean
def picEt (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
  -- lim over the poset of affine opens U ≤ T.left of PicEtAff C (T restricted to U),
  -- i.e. compatible families (λ_U)_U; CommGroup pointwise
def picEtFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}
def picEtUnit : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C
theorem picEt_affine_iso (hT : IsAffine T.left) : picEt C T ≃* PicEtAff C T ⋯
```

11	/-!
12	# Presented étale covers of an affine base
13	
14	A (singleton, affine) *étale cover* of `Spec A` is a faithfully flat étale `A`-algebra `B`.
15	For the étale-sheafification (plus) construction of the relative Picard functor, the covers
16	of a fixed base must form a *small* directed index: this file realizes them as **presented**
17	covers — a number of variables `n` together with an ideal of `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A` whose
18	quotient is étale over `A` with `Spec` mapping onto `Spec A`.  The type of presented covers
19	of `A` lives in the same universe as `A`, while still capturing every étale cover up to
20	isomorphism of the carrier (`Algebra.EtaleCover.of` and its accessor `ofEquiv`).
21	
22	Surjectivity of the spectrum map is recorded instead of faithful flatness because it is
23	statable without flatness hypotheses; combined with flatness of étale algebras it *is*
24	faithful flatness (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_comap_surjective`), and that instance is
25	provided on the carrier.
26	
27	## Main declarations
28	
29	* `Algebra.EtaleCover A`: presented étale covers of `Spec A`, a `Type u` for `A : Type u`;
30	  `E.Carrier` is the covering algebra, with `Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier` and
31	  `Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier` instances.
32	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.of B hB`: any étale `A`-algebra `B` (with surjective spectrum map)
33	  underlies a presented cover, with carrier identification `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofEquiv`.
34	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.Refines`: `E'` refines `E` when the covering spectrum of `E'` maps
35	  to that of `E` over the base — a mere existence (`Prop`); the plus construction proves
36	  independence of the chosen refinement map, so no choice of map is carried here.
37	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.prod`: the common refinement `Spec (B ⊗[A] B')` of two covers, with
38	  refinement witnesses `prodInl`/`prodInr` — directedness of the index
39	  (`exists_refines_prod`).
40	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.self`: the trivial cover `Spec A` itself, refined by every cover
41	  (`refines_self`) — the base point of the index.
42	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChange`: the pulled-back cover along `A → A'`, with carrier
43	  `A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier` (`baseChangeEquiv`) and the canonical `A`-algebra map
44	  `baseChangeInclude` into it.
45	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`: over a field `K`, every cover
46	  is refined by a finite separable field extension of `K` (single-factor refinement) —
47	  field-extension covers are cofinal, the form the degree theory and Galois descent
48	  consume; `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField` packages such an extension as a cover.
49	-/
50	
51	set_option autoImplicit false
52	
53	universe u
54	
55	open TensorProduct
56	
57	namespace Algebra
58	
59	/-- A presented étale cover of `Spec A`: a finite-variable polynomial presentation of an
60	étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum maps onto `Spec A`.  Presentations keep the type of covers
61	small (`Type u` for `A : Type u`), which is what makes the étale plus construction over
62	these covers a legitimate colimit; the carrier-level content is recovered by
63	`Algebra.EtaleCover.of`/`ofEquiv`. -/
64	structure EtaleCover (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : Type u where
65	  /-- The number of variables of the presentation. -/
66	  n : ℕ
67	  /-- The ideal of relations of the presentation. -/
68	  ideal : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
69	  /-- The presented algebra is étale over the base. -/
70	  etale : Algebra.Etale A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)
71	  /-- The spectrum of the presented algebra covers the spectrum of the base. -/
72	  comap_surjective :
73	    Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)))
74	
75	namespace EtaleCover
76	
77	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
78	
79	/-- The covering algebra presented by an étale cover. -/
80	protected abbrev Carrier (E : EtaleCover A) : Type u :=
81	  MvPolynomial (Fin E.n) A ⧸ E.ideal
82	
83	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier :=
84	  E.etale
85	
86	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier :=
87	  .of_comap_surjective E.comap_surjective
88	
89	/-! ## Constructors -/
90	
91	section constructors
92	
93	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
94	
95	/-- Package an explicitly presented étale algebra with surjective spectrum map as a
96	presented étale cover: the ideal of relations is the kernel of the presenting
97	surjection. -/
98	noncomputable def ofSurjective
99	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
100	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
101	    EtaleCover A where
102	  n := n
103	  ideal := RingHom.ker f
104	  etale := .of_equiv (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).symm
105	  comap_surjective := by
106	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A B := .of_comap_surjective hB
107	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ RingHom.ker f) :=
108	      .of_linearEquiv A B (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).toLinearEquiv
109	    exact PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
110	
111	/-- The carrier of `ofSurjective` is the presented algebra. -/
112	noncomputable def ofSurjectiveEquiv
113	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
114	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
115	    (ofSurjective hB f hf).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] B :=
116	  Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf
117	
118	/-- Any étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum covers `Spec A` underlies a presented étale
119	cover.  The presentation is chosen (étale algebras are finitely presented, in particular
120	finitely generated); the choice is harmless because consumers only ever use the carrier
121	identification `ofEquiv`. -/
122	noncomputable def of (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
123	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B))) : EtaleCover A :=
124	  ofSurjective hB
125	    (Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''.mp inferInstance).choose_spec.choose
126	    (Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''.mp inferInstance).choose_spec.choose_spec
127	
128	/-- The carrier of `of B hB` is `B` itself. -/
129	noncomputable def ofEquiv (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
130	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B))) :
131	    (of B hB).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] B :=
132	  ofSurjectiveEquiv hB _ _
133	
134	end constructors
135	
136	/-! ## Refinement and directedness -/
137	
138	/-- `E'` refines `E`: the covering spectrum of `E'` maps to that of `E` over `Spec A`,
139	i.e. there is an `A`-algebra map from the carrier of `E` to that of `E'`.  This is a mere
140	existence: the plus construction proves that the induced maps on descent classes do not
141	depend on the chosen refinement map, so no map is carried here. -/
142	def Refines (E' E : EtaleCover A) : Prop :=
143	  Nonempty (E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E'.Carrier)
144	
145	theorem refines_refl (E : EtaleCover A) : E.Refines E :=
146	  ⟨AlgHom.id A E.Carrier⟩
147	
148	theorem Refines.trans {E E' E'' : EtaleCover A} (h : E''.Refines E') (h' : E'.Refines E) :
149	    E''.Refines E := by
150	  obtain ⟨f⟩ := h
151	  obtain ⟨g⟩ := h'
152	  exact ⟨f.comp g⟩
153	
154	/-- The common refinement of two covers: `Spec` of the tensor product of the carriers,
155	i.e. the fiber product of the covering spectra over the base. -/
156	noncomputable def prod (E E' : EtaleCover A) : EtaleCover A :=
157	  haveI : Algebra.Etale A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
158	    Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
159	  haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
160	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
161	  .of (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
162	
163	/-- The carrier of the common refinement is the tensor product of the carriers. -/
164	noncomputable def prodEquiv (E E' : EtaleCover A) :
165	    (E.prod E').Carrier ≃ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier :=
166	  haveI : Algebra.Etale A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
167	    Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
168	  haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
169	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
170	  ofEquiv (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
171	
172	/-- The first refinement map of the common refinement. -/
173	noncomputable def prodInl (E E' : EtaleCover A) : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.prod E').Carrier :=
174	  ((E.prodEquiv E').symm.toAlgHom).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
175	
176	/-- The second refinement map of the common refinement. -/
177	noncomputable def prodInr (E E' : EtaleCover A) : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.prod E').Carrier :=
178	  ((E.prodEquiv E').symm.toAlgHom).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
179	
180	/-- Combine refinement maps out of the two factors into one out of the common
181	refinement (the universal property of the fiber product of the covering spectra). -/
182	noncomputable def prodLift {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
183	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (E.prod E').Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier :=
184	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift f g fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _).comp
185	    (E.prodEquiv E').toAlgHom
186	
187	@[simp]
188	theorem prodLift_comp_prodInl {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
189	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (prodLift f g).comp (E.prodInl E') = f := by
190	  ext x
191	  simp [prodLift, prodInl]
192	
193	@[simp]
194	theorem prodLift_comp_prodInr {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
195	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (prodLift f g).comp (E.prodInr E') = g := by
196	  ext x
197	  simp [prodLift, prodInr]
198	
199	theorem prod_refines_left (E E' : EtaleCover A) : (E.prod E').Refines E :=
200	  ⟨E.prodInl E'⟩
201	
202	theorem prod_refines_right (E E' : EtaleCover A) : (E.prod E').Refines E' :=
203	  ⟨E.prodInr E'⟩
204	
205	/-- Directedness of the refinement preorder: any two covers have a common refinement. -/
206	theorem exists_refines_prod (E E' : EtaleCover A) :
207	    ∃ E'' : EtaleCover A, E''.Refines E ∧ E''.Refines E' :=
208	  ⟨E.prod E', E.prod_refines_left E', E.prod_refines_right E'⟩
209	
210	/-- The trivial cover of `Spec A` by itself. -/
211	noncomputable def self (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : EtaleCover A :=
212	  .of A (by
213	    rw [show algebraMap A A = RingHom.id A from rfl, PrimeSpectrum.comap_id]
214	    exact fun p => ⟨p, rfl⟩)
215	
216	/-- The carrier of the trivial cover is the base ring. -/
217	noncomputable def selfEquiv (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : (self A).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] A :=
218	  ofEquiv A _
219	
220	/-- The canonical refinement map from the trivial cover to any cover (algebra side: the
221	structure map of the carrier, through the trivial carrier's identification with `A`). -/
222	noncomputable def fromSelf (E : EtaleCover A) : (self A).Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier :=
223	  (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).comp (selfEquiv A).toAlgHom
224	
225	/-- Every cover refines the trivial cover: the trivial cover is the base point of the
226	refinement preorder. -/
227	theorem refines_self (E : EtaleCover A) : E.Refines (self A) :=
228	  ⟨E.fromSelf⟩
229	
230	/-! ## Base change -/
231	
232	section baseChange
233	
234	variable (A' : Type u) [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A']
235	
236	/-- The base change of a cover along `A → A'`: the cover of `Spec A'` with carrier
237	`A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier` (the fiber product of the covering spectrum with the new base). -/
238	noncomputable def baseChange (E : EtaleCover A) : EtaleCover A' :=
239	  .of (A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
240	
241	/-- The carrier of the base-changed cover is the base-changed carrier. -/
242	noncomputable def baseChangeEquiv (E : EtaleCover A) :
243	    (E.baseChange A').Carrier ≃ₐ[A'] A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
244	  ofEquiv (A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
245	
246	/-- The canonical map from the carrier of a cover to the carrier of its base change,
247	as a map of `A`-algebras. -/
248	noncomputable def baseChangeInclude (E : EtaleCover A) :
249	    E.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.baseChange A').Carrier :=
250	  (((E.baseChangeEquiv A').symm.toAlgHom).restrictScalars A).comp
251	    Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
252	
253	end baseChange
254	
255	/-! ## Covers of a field: single-factor refinement -/
256	
257	section field
258	
259	variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
260	
261	/-- The carrier of a cover of a field (indeed, of any nontrivial base) is nontrivial. -/
262	theorem nontrivial_carrier (E : EtaleCover A) [Nontrivial A] : Nontrivial E.Carrier :=
263	  PrimeSpectrum.nonempty_iff_nontrivial.mp
264	    ⟨(E.comap_surjective (Nonempty.some inferInstance)).choose⟩
265	
266	/-- **Field cofinality**: over a field, every presented étale cover is refined by a finite
267	separable field extension.  This single-factor refinement is what makes field-extension
268	covers cofinal among étale covers of `Spec K`: the étale carrier is a finite product of
269	finite separable extensions of `K`, and projection to any one factor still covers the
270	(one-point) spectrum of `K`. -/
271	theorem exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom (E : EtaleCover K) :
272	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L)
273	      (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L), Nonempty (E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L) := by
274	  haveI : Nontrivial E.Carrier := E.nontrivial_carrier
275	  obtain ⟨I, hI, Ai, hfield, halg, e, h⟩ :=
276	    (Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod K E.Carrier).mp inferInstance
277	  haveI : Nonempty I := by
278	    by_contra hempty
279	    haveI : IsEmpty I := not_nonempty_iff.mp hempty
280	    haveI : Subsingleton E.Carrier := e.toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mpr inferInstance
281	    exact false_of_nontrivial_of_subsingleton E.Carrier
282	  obtain ⟨i⟩ := ‹Nonempty I›
283	  exact ⟨Ai i, hfield i, halg i, (h i).1, (h i).2,
284	    ⟨(Pi.evalAlgHom K Ai i).comp e.toAlgHom⟩⟩
285	
286	variable (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
287	
288	instance : Algebra.Etale K L where
289	  formallyEtale := Algebra.FormallyEtale.of_isSeparable K L
290	  finitePresentation :=
291	    (Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType (R := K) (A := L)).mp inferInstance
292	
293	/-- A finite separable field extension as an étale cover of `Spec K` (the spectrum map
294	between the one-point spectra is trivially surjective). -/
295	noncomputable def ofField : EtaleCover K :=
296	  .of L fun _ => ⟨default, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
297	
298	/-- The carrier of the field cover is the field extension itself. -/
299	noncomputable def ofFieldEquiv : (ofField (K := K) L).Carrier ≃ₐ[K] L :=

301	
302	end field

12	The étale sheafification of the relative Picard functor is computed over *affine* test
13	objects, where a test object is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra `A` (the landed
14	`AlgebraicGeometry.overSpec k A : Over (Spec k)`) and a test map is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra
15	map.  This file provides the algebra-indexed face of the relative Picard functor:
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.overSpecMap f`: `Spec` of a `k`-algebra map `f : A →ₐ[k] B`, as a
18	  morphism `overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A` of `Over (Spec k)`, strictly functorial
19	  (`overSpecMap_id`, `overSpecMap_comp`).
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap C f`: restriction of relative Picard classes along
21	  `Spec f`, a group homomorphism `relPic C (overSpec k A) →* relPic C (overSpec k B)`,
22	  covariantly functorial in the algebra (`relPicAlgMap_id`, `relPicAlgMap_comp`).
23	
24	The étale plus construction (`Picard/PicEtAff.lean`) consumes only this interface: descent
25	classes on an étale cover are an equalizer of two `relPicAlgMap`s, and all refinement
26	transports are `relPicAlgMap`s of `A`-algebra maps restricted to `k`.
27	-/

37	section OverSpecMap
38	
39	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
40	variable {A B C' D : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
41	  [CommRing C'] [Algebra k C'] [CommRing D] [Algebra k D]

43	/-- `Spec` of a `k`-algebra map, as a morphism of `Over (Spec k)`. -/
44	noncomputable def Over.overSpecMap (f : A →ₐ[k] B) : overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A :=
45	  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f.toRingHom)) (by
46	    dsimp
47	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, AlgHom.comp_algebraMap])
48	
49	@[simp]
50	lemma Over.overSpecMap_left (f : A →ₐ[k] B) :
51	    (Over.overSpecMap f).left = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f.toRingHom) :=
52	  rfl
53	
54	private lemma spec_map_id_alg :
55	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (AlgHom.id k A).toRingHom) = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) := by
56	  rw [show CommRingCat.ofHom (AlgHom.id k A).toRingHom = 𝟙 (CommRingCat.of A) from rfl,
57	    Spec.map_id]
58	
59	private lemma spec_map_comp_alg (f : A →ₐ[k] B) (g : B →ₐ[k] C') :
60	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (g.comp f).toRingHom)
61	      = (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom g.toRingHom) :
62	            Spec (CommRingCat.of C') ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of B))
63	          ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f.toRingHom) := by
64	  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
65	  rfl
66	
67	@[simp]
68	lemma Over.overSpecMap_id : Over.overSpecMap (AlgHom.id k A) = 𝟙 (overSpec k A) := by
69	  ext : 1
70	  exact spec_map_id_alg
71	
72	@[simp]
73	lemma Over.overSpecMap_comp (f : A →ₐ[k] B) (g : B →ₐ[k] C') :
74	    Over.overSpecMap (g.comp f) = Over.overSpecMap g ≫ Over.overSpecMap f := by
75	  ext : 1
76	  exact spec_map_comp_alg f g

78	end OverSpecMap

80	section RelPicAlgMap

82	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
83	variable {A B C' : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
84	  [CommRing C'] [Algebra k C']
85	
86	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along `Spec` of a `k`-algebra map: the
87	algebra-indexed face of the relative Picard functor, covariant in the algebra. -/
88	noncomputable def relPicAlgMap (f : A →ₐ[k] B) :
89	    relPic C (overSpec k A) →* relPic C (overSpec k B) :=
90	  relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap f)
91	
92	@[simp]
93	lemma relPicAlgMap_id (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
94	    relPicAlgMap C (AlgHom.id k A) x = x := by
95	  rw [relPicAlgMap, Over.overSpecMap_id]
96	  exact relPicMap_id C x
97	
98	lemma relPicAlgMap_comp (f : A →ₐ[k] B) (g : B →ₐ[k] C') (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
99	    relPicAlgMap C (g.comp f) x = relPicAlgMap C g (relPicAlgMap C f x) := by
100	  rw [relPicAlgMap, Over.overSpecMap_comp]
101	  exact relPicMap_comp C (Over.overSpecMap f) (Over.overSpecMap g) x
102	
103	end RelPicAlgMap
